purpose: Record what this fixed material actually contains and what it does not, so later reading does not mistake an abstraction-only or citation-only boundary for a missing proof. No correctness judgement, no formula repair, no added hypothesis.
what_the_source_contains: A complete 8-section paper plus an appendix, with a complete proof of Theorem 8.1 at native 2330-2332 (printed 240).

Section 1 (native 272-424, printed 188-193) is a ten-subsection introduction: purity and regularity, Bertin's non-Noetherian regularity and Prüfer domains, the Auslander-Buchsbaum formula for general local rings, Basic setup I, purity for torsors on smooth relative curves, Zariski-Nagata over Prüfer bases, Basic setup II, Grothendieck-Serre for quasi-split groups, Nisnevich's purity conjecture for quasi-split groups, and notations. Acknowledgements at 417-424.

Section 2 (425-959, printed 193-205) builds coherent schemes, reflexive sheaves, depths, associated primes, weak dimensions and coherent regular rings, and proves the purity of reflexive sheaves over regular coherent rings (2.19, 2.21, 2.22) with full proofs (native 800-905).

Section 3 (960-1190, printed 205-210) collects the geometry over Prüfer bases: 3.2 (fibre-codimension bookkeeping with 4 labelled clauses), 3.4 (finite-dimensional approximation of a semilocal Prüfer domain), 3.5 (Cesnavicius' Variant 3.7 in the Prüferian setting), plus 3.6-3.13 on regularity and reflexive sheaves, all proved.

Section 4 (1191-1438, printed 210-216) proves Auslander's flatness criterion (4.1) through a length function on torsion modules (4.3, the map l), four homological lemmas (4.5-4.7) and the two-case induction of 4.8 (printed 213-216), together with the length estimates in 4.2 and the appendix-facing input A.6.

Section 5 (1439-1585, printed 216-220) is the torsor toolkit: definition of G-torsors and trivialisations (5.2), descent data (5.5) with its tikzcd cocycle diagram, Isom-sheaf lemma (5.4), descent lemma (5.6) and the equivalence criterion (5.7).

Section 6 (1586-1861, printed 220-226) proves purity for torsors on relative curves (6.2, 6.3), the local variant (6.5), the generic-triviality extension corollary (6.6, attributed to GL23 Cor. 2.10), purity for finite locally free groups (6.8) and Zariski-Nagata for finite étale covers (6.9), all with complete proofs.

Section 7 (1862-2134, printed 227-234) develops parafactorial pairs (7.1-7.4), the fppf local cohomology of tori (7.5-7.8), purity for groups of multiplicative type (7.9) and the Grothendieck-Serre type results for multiplicative-type groups (7.11, two scenarios).

Section 8 (2135-2333, printed 234-240) is the retained unit's section: Theorem 8.1 with its two clauses, the geometric input 8.2, the torsor-lifting reduction 8.3, the group-equating lemma 8.4 for geometrically unibranch semilocal rings, and the three curve replacements 8.5-8.7, then the closing proof of 8.1 at 2330-2332.

Appendix (2334-2523, printed 240-244) proves the coherent-regular facts used in the body: ff-descent (A.1), étale-locality (A.2 and Claim A.2.1), the fibre criterion (A.3), the flat-regular-map corollary (A.4), the ring-map example (A.5), the linear-algebra lemma A.6, the Auslander-Buchsbaum formula A.7 and the wdim = depth corollary A.8.
The complete bibliography machinery: 45 distinct \cite keys used 128 times, all resolving to 45 printed entries on printed 244-246.
what_the_source_does_not_contain: No figure, no table, no \includegraphics and no tikzpicture. The only graphical objects are 5 tikzcd commutative diagrams inside the torsor-descent material.

No proof environment for 2.24, 3.4, 4.1, 4.8.5, 5.2, 5.3, 5.5, 6.4, 6.5, 6.6, 7.7, 7.11, 8.4, A.4 and A.5 (15 of the 71 numbered positions). Their status differs and is recorded per item in DIFFICULTY_SCREENING.json's proof_gap_dispositions: 4.1's proof is section 4.8 (printed 213-216); 8.4 is quoted from Ces22a Lem. 5.1 with the Noetherian hypothesis noted as unused; 6.6 is quoted from GL23 Cor. 2.10; 6.5, A.4 and A.5 are stated as consequences with the derivation indicated in prose; the remaining ones are definitions, remarks, a corollary deduced from 7.9/7.11, and the Claim 4.8.5 which is literally cited to the Stacks Project tag 057F.
No separate technical section or second appendix: the paper has exactly 8 numbered sections plus one appendix.
No compiled project: cedram.cls, mathalfa, extpfeil, colonequals, cleveref, jepalpha(+eid).bst and both .bib files are missing locally.

No author-side statement of novelty for Theorem 8.1: the introduction at 367-375 and the section-8 opening at 2135-2137 present it as following the strategy of Ces22a and as a Prüferian version of the Nisnevich conjecture inspired by Ces22b, which treats Dedekind R. Whether that constitutes a new problem is not settled by the file.

standard_prerequisites: Grothendieck-Serre conjecture in the quasi-split case over a semilocal Prüfer scheme (used through GL23 Th. A.0.1 in the proof of 8.3).

Purity for reductive torsors over regular local rings of dimension 2 (Colliot-Thelene-Sansuc, cited at 294-295 as CTS79 Th. 6.13) and the Auslander-Buchsbaum formula in the Noetherian case (AB57 Th. 3.7).
fppf descent for torsors and the standard theory of reductive group schemes with quasi-pinnings (SGA3IIInew Exp. XXVI).
Valuative criterion of properness and the standard limit/Noetherian-approximation machinery, used at 368 and inside 8.3.
These are cited, not re-proved, in accordance with the rule that standard prerequisites may be cited accurately without recursive re-proof.
